title: Fossil Trees
text: Fossil Trees. During the progress of the works for reclaiming the extensive waste called White Moss, between Middleton and Failsworth, a large number of trees, of enormous magnitude, have been discovered at a depth of about six feet; some of the oaks have been nearly twelve feet in girth and forty feet in length. Several trees of the oak, fir, and yew tribe have been found to be thoroughly sound, even to the outermost part. Many of the oak-trees have proved proved more tough and flexible than this tree is under ordinary circumstances. A large quantity of the timber has most unquestionably been on fire. It seems that during some remote age the fossil-trees at White Moss have been burnt, for there are examples of the main shaft of these timbers having been consumed. Singular as it may appear, the trees found in this moss have invariably been met with lying in a direction either south-east or due east.
